boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain United States Military Academy
boards.description: Ten under-21-safe food and snack destinations with published evening availability on post or in nearby Highland Falls and New Windsor.

cards.title: Grant Hall Marketplace
cards.subtitle: Grant Hall, West Point
cards.notes: Check the weekend schedule before heading over; the Marketplace lists pizza, burritos, sandwiches, soups, coffee, and other casual options.
cards.short_summary: A campus dining option with weekend service into the evening.
cards.evidence_claim: West Point lists Grant Hall Marketplace in Grant Hall and publishes Saturday–Sunday hours of 11 a.m.–9:30 p.m.
cards.source_title: Day in the Life | U.S. Military Academy West Point
cards.access_notes: Published weekend hours run until 9:30 p.m.; confirm access rules and operating changes with West Point.

cards.title: West Point Bowling Alley
cards.subtitle: Near Buffalo Soldier Field, West Point
cards.notes: Use the bowling-alley snack counter for an evening food-and-beverage stop, and verify lane or facility access before making the trip.
cards.short_summary: An on-post snack stop with the latest listed weekend hours in this set.
cards.evidence_claim: West Point states that the Bowling Alley near Buffalo Soldier Field sells snacks and beverages and is open until 11 p.m. Friday and Saturday.
cards.source_title: Day in the Life | U.S. Military Academy West Point
cards.access_notes: Published hours are until 11 p.m. Friday and Saturday; check facility access and schedule changes before going.

cards.title: Hacienda Restaurant
cards.subtitle: 145 Main St, Highland Falls
cards.notes: Place a pickup or delivery order through the restaurant’s site, then use its posted day-specific schedule to time an evening meal.
cards.short_summary: A Main Street pickup-and-delivery option open latest on Friday and Saturday.
cards.evidence_claim: Hacienda Restaurant’s official ordering page lists takeout hours until 11 p.m. Friday and Saturday at 145 Main St, Highland Falls.
cards.access_notes: Takeout is listed until 11 p.m. Friday–Saturday and until 10 p.m. on other listed open days; Tuesday is closed.

cards.title: Park Restaurant
cards.subtitle: 451 Main St, Highland Falls
cards.notes: Plan a seated dinner or check directly for service details; the restaurant identifies its space as family-friendly and publishes evening closing times.
cards.short_summary: A family-friendly Main Street restaurant with late Friday and Saturday hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Park Restaurant’s official site describes a family-friendly space at 451 Main St and lists hours until 11:30 p.m. Friday and Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Published hours are until 11 p.m. Monday–Thursday and 11:30 p.m. Friday–Saturday; Sunday is closed.

cards.title: West Point Pizza
cards.subtitle: 282 Main St, Highland Falls
cards.notes: Use the restaurant’s online-ordering option or call ahead, especially close to closing; its site also states it delivers to West Point and Highland Falls.
cards.short_summary: A seven-day Main Street pizza option with delivery coverage stated for West Point.
cards.evidence_claim: West Point Pizza’s official site lists daily 11 a.m.–10 p.m. hours at 282 Main St and states delivery service includes West Point.
cards.access_notes: The official site lists service every day until 10 p.m.; verify delivery availability and cutoff times directly.

cards.title: Delizia's Pizza Kitchen
cards.subtitle: 287 Main St, Highland Falls
cards.notes: Order online or call before leaving campus, using the listed daily hours as the outer limit rather than assuming late orders are accepted.
cards.short_summary: A daily Highland Falls pizza-kitchen option with a published 10 p.m. close.
cards.evidence_claim: Delizia’s Pizza Kitchen’s official site lists its Highland Falls location at 287 Main St and hours of 11 a.m.–10 p.m. every day.
cards.access_notes: Published daily hours run until 10 p.m.; confirm kitchen and pickup cutoff times before traveling.

cards.title: McDonald's on W Point Hwy
cards.subtitle: 104 W Point Hwy, Highland Falls
cards.notes: Use the official location page to check restaurant and drive-through availability for the day, then order through the listed mobile-order option if useful.
cards.short_summary: A nearby chain location with published 11 p.m. restaurant and drive-through hours.
cards.evidence_claim: McDonald’s official location page for 104 W Point Hwy lists restaurant and drive-through hours until 11 p.m. daily.
cards.source_title: McDonald's | 104 W Point Hwy, Highland Falls
cards.access_notes: The official page lists restaurant and drive-through service until 11 p.m. daily; verify holiday changes before departing.

cards.title: Tosco's Pizzeria Restaurant
cards.subtitle: 434 Blooming Grove Tpke, New Windsor
cards.notes: Use the New Windsor location page when planning a later pickup; it separates the extended Friday–Saturday schedule from weekday and Sunday hours.
cards.short_summary: A New Windsor pizza destination with 11 p.m. Friday and Saturday hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Tosco’s official New Windsor page lists 434 Blooming Grove Tpke and hours until 11 p.m. on Friday and Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Friday–Saturday hours are listed until 11 p.m.; Monday–Thursday and Sunday are listed until 10 p.m.

cards.title: ABC Pizza & Restaurant
cards.subtitle: 198 Quassaick Ave, New Windsor
cards.notes: Call or use the restaurant’s contact details before a late pickup; its location page presents this as a family-owned, family-operated restaurant.
cards.short_summary: A New Windsor family-operated pizza-and-restaurant stop with 11 p.m. published hours.
cards.evidence_claim: ABC Pizza & Restaurant’s official location page lists 198 Quassaick Ave, New Windsor and business hours until 11 p.m. Monday–Sunday.
cards.source_title: ABC Pizza & Restaurant | New Windsor Location
cards.access_notes: Its official location page lists service until 11 p.m. daily; confirm current pickup timing before leaving.

cards.title: Farmers Deli N Grill
cards.subtitle: 904 Little Britain Rd, New Windsor
cards.notes: Check the restaurant’s ordering page before heading out, since it lists full hours and notes that online ordering may be temporarily unavailable.
cards.short_summary: A New Windsor deli and grill with an 11 p.m. published closing time.
cards.evidence_claim: Farmers Deli N Grill’s official page lists 904 Little Britain Rd, New Windsor and hours of 6 a.m.–11 p.m.
cards.source_title: Farmers Deli N Grill | New Windsor
cards.access_notes: The official page lists hours until 11 p.m.; it also says online ordering is temporarily paused, so call ahead if needed.

boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: A practical look at named West Point spaces tied to cadet study, meals, athletics, presentations, and Corps events.

cards.title: Jefferson Library
cards.subtitle: Library coffee stop and academic break space
cards.notes: Use an academic break to work on an assignment, consult a professor, or pause at the ground-floor coffee café; follow current building-access rules.
cards.short_summary: An official cadet-day account names the library as a place for coffee and assignment work between classes.
cards.evidence_claim: West Point says cadets use breaks in morning classes to enjoy coffee in Jefferson Library and work on assignments.
cards.source_title: Day in the Life of a Cadet
cards.access_notes: Campus access and library rules apply; verify access before visiting.

cards.title: Grant Hall
cards.subtitle: Casual dining in a long-running social venue
cards.notes: Plan a low-key break from the mess hall here when it is open, and check the current dining schedule before relying on it.
cards.short_summary: The Academy describes Grant Hall as a central social venue with casual dining for cadets.
cards.evidence_claim: West Point calls Grant Hall a central social venue for over a century and says it offers casual dining for cadets taking a break from the mess hall.
cards.source_title: Day in the Life of a Cadet
cards.access_notes: Dining availability and campus access may vary; confirm current hours.

cards.title: Cadet Mess Hall
cards.subtitle: Family-style meals with cadet companies
cards.notes: Treat meals as scheduled community time: cadets sit at assigned tables with friends from their companies, so arrive according to the Academy schedule.
cards.short_summary: The mess hall is the setting for the Academy’s scheduled family-style breakfast and lunch.
cards.evidence_claim: West Point states that breakfast and lunch are eaten family style in the mess hall, with cadets at assigned tables with friends from their cadet companies.
cards.source_title: Day in the Life of a Cadet
cards.access_notes: Cadet dining procedures and visitor access are controlled; verify eligibility in advance.

cards.title: Arvin Cadet Physical Development Center
cards.subtitle: Venue for company athletics
cards.notes: Look for scheduled company-athletics activity here and use only authorized programs or access; the facility hosted basketball, fitness, and grappling championship events.
cards.short_summary: Arvin is documented as a host site for Corps company-athletics championship competition.
cards.evidence_claim: West Point reported that fall brigade championships, including basketball, functional fitness, and submission grappling, took place at Arvin Cadet Physical Development Center.
cards.source_title: Company teams fight, earn fall brigade titles
cards.access_notes: Use requires authorized facility access and adherence to current athletics policies.

cards.title: Daly Field
cards.subtitle: Company-athletics field venue
cards.notes: Check the Academy athletics calendar for a scheduled contest or company event, then watch or participate only through approved access and program channels.
cards.short_summary: Daly Field is a documented venue for company soccer and flag-football championship activity.
cards.evidence_claim: West Point reported that fall brigade championships in soccer and flag football took place at Daly Field.
cards.source_title: Company teams fight, earn fall brigade titles
cards.access_notes: Field access depends on Academy scheduling and authorization.

cards.title: Eisenhower Hall
cards.subtitle: Cadet speaker-series and ceremony venue
cards.notes: Watch for a public or authorized Academy talk here; West Point has used the hall for cadet Q&A sessions with visiting national-security speakers.
cards.short_summary: Eisenhower Hall hosts cadet-facing presentations and major Academy gatherings.
cards.evidence_claim: The Modern War Institute reported that FBI Director Christopher Wray addressed West Point’s first- and second-class cadets at Eisenhower Hall and joined a cadet Q&A.
cards.source_title: MWI Speaker Series: Hon. Christopher Wray, FBI Director
cards.access_notes: Entry is event- and access-dependent; verify event eligibility and security requirements.

cards.title: Robinson Auditorium
cards.subtitle: Cadet debate and speaker setting in Thayer Hall
cards.notes: When an authorized lecture or debate is scheduled, arrive with enough time for campus entry procedures and use the event listing for room details.
cards.short_summary: Cadets have gathered in Robinson Auditorium for an Academy-hosted debate.
cards.evidence_claim: The Modern War Institute reported that cadets and faculty gathered in Robinson Auditorium for a cadet-led debate during its inaugural Sandhurst Conference.
cards.access_notes: Auditorium access is limited to scheduled events and authorized attendees.

cards.title: Thayer Hall
cards.subtitle: Academic hall with cadet research activity
cards.notes: Use the building for scheduled classes, research meetings, or academic events; the Digital History Center identifies its location in Thayer Hall.
cards.short_summary: Thayer Hall is a documented home for West Point digital-history work involving cadet research.
cards.evidence_claim: West Point’s Digital History Center says its work includes cadet research with faculty mentorship and lists its location as Thayer Hall, Department of History, Room 151.
cards.access_notes: Academic building access is controlled; coordinate through the relevant department or event.

cards.title: The Plain
cards.subtitle: Parade-ground landmark in cadet life
cards.notes: View it from authorized campus areas and consult the Academy calendar for formal formations or ceremonies; do not enter restricted event space.
cards.short_summary: The Plain is a named landmark associated with cadet marching and Academy ceremonies.
cards.evidence_claim: West Point Press states that every cadet who marches across the Plain today follows in Sylvanus Thayer’s footsteps.
cards.access_notes: Observe campus security directions and any event perimeter or access restrictions.

cards.title: Mahan Hall
cards.subtitle: Academic-event location for cadet engineering work
cards.notes: Use the posted event or department contact to confirm a meeting or presentation in this hall; do not assume walk-in access to academic rooms.
cards.short_summary: Mahan Hall has hosted cadet presentations and working groups in a tactical-innovation symposium.
cards.evidence_claim: A West Point tactical innovation symposium agenda lists cadet presentations and working groups in Mahan Hall, including projects by first-year mechanical engineering cadets.
cards.access_notes: Mahan Hall access and room use are authorization-dependent.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten no-admission activities at the free West Point Museum, just outside Thayer Gate.

cards.title: West Point Museum
cards.subtitle: Olmsted Hall, Pershing Center
cards.notes: Meet at the museum entrance, then choose a gallery to explore together at your own pace. Confirm the day’s opening before leaving.
cards.short_summary: A self-paced history stop with free admission.
cards.evidence_claim: The official Army Museum Enterprise page lists the West Point Museum at 2110 New South Post Road and states “Free Admission.”
cards.source_title: West Point Museum | U.S. Army Center of Military History
cards.access_notes: Open Tuesday–Sunday, 10:00–16:00; closed Monday and listed holidays. Located adjacent to the Visitor Center, outside Thayer Gate.

cards.title: Trace the History of West Point exhibit
cards.subtitle: West Point Museum
cards.notes: Start with the Revolutionary War section and follow the display’s timeline through the Academy’s history; compare one detail each before moving on.
cards.short_summary: A chronological museum-gallery walk.
cards.evidence_claim: The museum’s official exhibit description says this display chronicles the West Point garrison and the United States Military Academy, beginning in the Revolutionary War.
cards.source_title: West Point Museum | U.S. Army Center of Military History
cards.access_notes: Included with the museum’s free admission; visit during posted museum hours.

cards.title: Walk the Large Weapons exhibit
cards.subtitle: Lower level, West Point Museum
cards.notes: Use the lower-level displays as a slow loop: identify an artillery piece, the tank, and one artwork that catches your attention.
cards.short_summary: Oversize equipment and art on the museum’s lower level.
cards.evidence_claim: The official museum page identifies a Large Weapons exhibit on the lowest level, with artillery pieces and a First World War tank.
cards.source_title: West Point Museum | U.S. Army Center of Military History
cards.access_notes: Included with the museum’s free admission; visit during posted museum hours.

cards.title: Follow the Small Weapons timeline
cards.subtitle: Balcony exhibit, West Point Museum
cards.notes: Take the balcony exhibit in sequence and pick a single change in design to discuss, from early clubs through modern automatic firearms.
cards.short_summary: A gallery tracing handheld weaponry across eras.
cards.evidence_claim: The official museum page says the Small Weapons balcony exhibit traces hand-held weaponry from the Stone Age club to modern automatic firearms.
cards.source_title: West Point Museum | U.S. Army Center of Military History
cards.access_notes: Included with the museum’s free admission; visit during posted museum hours.

cards.title: Study the D-Day veteran murals
cards.subtitle: Large Weapons exhibit, West Point Museum
cards.notes: Pause with both murals and look for contrasting details in the depictions of the 1944 Allied invasion of Europe.
cards.short_summary: Two large artworks tied to the Allied invasion of Europe.
cards.evidence_claim: The official museum page highlights two murals by a D-Day veteran depicting the Allied invasion of Europe in 1944.
cards.source_title: West Point Museum | U.S. Army Center of Military History
cards.access_notes: Included with the museum’s free admission; visit during posted museum hours.

cards.title: See the Nagasaki-type atomic bomb display
cards.subtitle: Large Weapons exhibit, West Point Museum
cards.notes: Approach this historical display deliberately, read its interpretation, and give the group time to reflect before continuing through the gallery.
cards.short_summary: A documented large-weapons display with historical context.
cards.evidence_claim: The official museum page lists an atomic bomb of the type dropped on Nagasaki among the Large Weapons exhibit highlights.
cards.source_title: West Point Museum | U.S. Army Center of Military History
cards.access_notes: Included with the museum’s free admission; visit during posted museum hours.

cards.title: Find the French 75-mm field gun
cards.subtitle: Large Weapons exhibit, West Point Museum
cards.notes: Locate the field gun, inspect its shield, and read the label together before comparing it with the other large artillery displays.
cards.short_summary: A field gun connected to the first American shot of World War I.
cards.evidence_claim: An official Army History feature identifies the museum’s French 75-mm field gun as having fired the first American shot against German troops on 23 October 1917.
cards.source_title: The West Point Museum First World War Centennial Commemoration Exhibits | Army History
cards.access_notes: Included with the museum’s free admission; visit during posted museum hours.

cards.title: Look over the Model 1917 tank
cards.subtitle: Large Weapons exhibit, West Point Museum
cards.notes: Circle the tank display from a respectful distance and use the label to connect its design to the First World War context.
cards.short_summary: A U.S. Model 1917 tank in the large-weapons gallery.
cards.evidence_claim: An official Army History feature says a U.S. Model 1917 Six-Ton Special Tractor is adjacent to the French 75-mm field gun in the museum’s Large Weapons gallery.
cards.source_title: The West Point Museum First World War Centennial Commemoration Exhibits | Army History
cards.access_notes: Included with the museum’s free admission; visit during posted museum hours.

cards.title: View George Washington’s pistols
cards.subtitle: West Point Museum
cards.notes: Find the pistols and read the provenance story together; keep the focus on the documented object rather than handling or reenactment.
cards.short_summary: A pair of documented Washington pistols in the museum collection.
cards.evidence_claim: An official Army History article states that George Washington’s pistols are at the West Point Museum and calls them among the best documented pistols he used.
cards.access_notes: Included with the museum’s free admission; visit during posted museum hours.

cards.entity_name: West Point and The Civil War
cards.title: Browse West Point and The Civil War
cards.subtitle: USMA Library online exhibit
cards.notes: Open the online exhibit together, choose one section from 1860–1865, and trade observations about the Academy’s Civil War-era perspective.
cards.short_summary: A free, web-based USMA Library exhibit.
cards.evidence_claim: The USMA Library describes “West Point and The Civil War” as an exhibit developed with the West Point Museum using Archives and Special Collections material.
cards.source_title: Browse Exhibits | U.S. Military Academy Library Exhibits
cards.access_notes: Available online; no admission or purchase is required to browse the public exhibit page.

boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten documented academic environments at West Point, from library workstations and facilitated writing support to research-centered study settings.

cards.entity_name: Thomas Jefferson Hall Library and Learning Center
cards.title: Thomas Jefferson Hall Library and Learning Center
cards.subtitle: 758 Cullum Road · West Point
cards.notes: Use this six-story academic hub when you need a library-centered work session; it includes more than 900 learning and study spaces.
cards.short_summary: A large library and learning center with extensive cadet workstation capacity.
cards.evidence_claim: The completed facility includes more than 900 learning and study spaces and serves as a hub for research, collaboration, and digital learning.
cards.source_title: USMA Thomas Jefferson Hall Library and Learning Center
cards.access_notes: Common-area eligibility is limited to authorized military, USMA/DoD-affiliated users, approved event attendees, and scheduled collection researchers; carry required identification.

cards.title: Alexander Haig Room
cards.subtitle: Top floor · Jefferson Hall Library
cards.notes: Use this formal room for group academic work only when it is not assigned to an event, lecture, reception, or other scheduled use.
cards.short_summary: A top-floor library room intended for both group study and academic learning.
cards.evidence_claim: The Alexander Haig Room is intended for group study and academic learning as well as events, lectures, and multimedia presentations.
cards.access_notes: Availability may be affected by receptions, special events, lectures, or multimedia presentations. Jefferson Hall access is restricted to eligible users or approved appointments.

cards.title: Mounger Writing Center
cards.subtitle: Second floor · Jefferson Hall
cards.notes: Bring a draft, assignment, or communications project and use a one-on-one consultation or workshop to move the work forward.
cards.short_summary: Writing-focused academic support located inside Jefferson Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: The Mounger Writing Center, on Jefferson Hall’s second floor, offers one-on-one consultations, group workshops, and special events for cadets’ writing and communications projects.
cards.access_notes: Services are described for cadets; arrange a consultation or attend a workshop as applicable. Jefferson Hall access is restricted to eligible users or approved appointments.

cards.title: Center for Enhanced Performance
cards.subtitle: Jefferson Hall Library and Learning Center
cards.notes: Use performance-strategy instruction to plan a focused study block, then apply its concentration and visualization techniques to your coursework.
cards.short_summary: Academic-performance support focused on mental skills and strategies.
cards.evidence_claim: The Center for Enhanced Performance helps cadets improve academic performance through targeted education and training in mental skills, including focus, concentration, visualization, and imagery.
cards.access_notes: The program is described for cadets; participation and appointment details should be confirmed with the center. Jefferson Hall access is restricted to eligible users or approved appointments.

cards.title: Operations Research Center
cards.subtitle: Mahan Hall · Systems Engineering
cards.notes: For an approved analytical project, ask your faculty adviser about connecting coursework to the center’s research and problem-solving activity.
cards.short_summary: A systems-engineering research setting for analytical work tied to national issues.
cards.evidence_claim: The Operations Research Center provides dedicated analytical capability that enriches cadet education and engages problems of national significance.
cards.access_notes: Housed in the Department of Systems Engineering; research participation is program- and faculty-coordinated rather than represented as general public access.

cards.title: Robotics Research Center
cards.subtitle: Electrical Engineering & Computer Science
cards.notes: If your work involves autonomous systems, pursue a faculty-connected research opportunity and use the center’s interdisciplinary project context.
cards.short_summary: A named research setting for cadet work in robotics and autonomous systems.
cards.evidence_claim: The Robotics Research Center provides cadets, staff, and faculty opportunities to conduct basic and applied research on robotics and autonomous systems.
cards.access_notes: Research access is tied to cadet, staff, faculty, and interdisciplinary project participation; contact the center or an EECS faculty member before planning a visit.

cards.title: Digital History Center
cards.subtitle: History & War Studies
cards.notes: Use a digital-history project to turn course research into a map, digital textbook contribution, or another faculty-supported historical resource.
cards.short_summary: A history-focused setting that supports cadet digital scholarship.
cards.evidence_claim: The Digital History Center supports faculty and cadets creating digital history products and digital resources that enhance cadet learning.
cards.access_notes: Housed in the Department of History & War Studies; use is connected to academic work and center-supported projects, so confirm participation with department staff.

cards.entity_name: Resnick Center for Holocaust and Genocide Studies
cards.title: Resnick Center for Holocaust and Genocide Studies
cards.subtitle: West Point academic center
cards.notes: Approach this center for faculty-supported research or learning resources on mass atrocity and its prevention, with care for the subject matter.
cards.short_summary: A research and teaching center for rigorous study of mass atrocity prevention.
cards.evidence_claim: The Resnick Center is a hub of teaching, research, and practice for military education and training about mass atrocity and its prevention.
cards.access_notes: Engage through its academic programming or faculty guidance; the source does not represent the center as a public drop-in study room.

cards.title: West Point Music Research Center
cards.subtitle: West Point Band research program
cards.notes: Use this research setting for an approved project on music, sound, identity, or data analysis, and connect with its workshops or academic resources.
cards.short_summary: A multidisciplinary research center focused on music, sound, and cultural identity.
cards.evidence_claim: The West Point Music Research Center supports cadet projects, conducts research, compiles literature, and facilitates workshops, lectures, and experiences.
cards.access_notes: Center activities support cadets, staff, and faculty; confirm project or program access directly with the center before visiting.

cards.entity_name: U.S. Army Space and Missile Defense Command Space and High-Altitude Research Center
cards.title: SMDC-SHARC
cards.subtitle: Physics & Nuclear Engineering · 606 Thayer Road
cards.notes: For a relevant space or missile-defense topic, ask the Physics and Nuclear Engineering department about research and education opportunities.
cards.short_summary: A physics-and-nuclear-engineering research center for space, high-altitude, and missile-defense study.
cards.evidence_claim: SMDC-SHARC provides space-operations education and directs space, high-altitude, and missile-defense research at West Point.
cards.access_notes: Housed in Physics and Nuclear Engineering at 606 Thayer Road; research use should be coordinated with the center or department rather than assumed as drop-in access.

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named destinations on Highland Falls’ Main Street corridor and the adjacent South Post approach, each with a directly sourced reason to stop.

cards.title: West Point Museum — public military-history exhibits
cards.subtitle: New South Post Road, beside the Main Street corridor
cards.notes: Walk the South Post approach to the public museum and use the galleries to connect Academy, Army, and military-history artifacts with the place itself.
cards.short_summary: A public museum focused on West Point, the Army, and the profession of arms.
cards.evidence_claim: The Army Museum Enterprise identifies the West Point Museum as a public institution that collects, preserves, exhibits, and interprets artifacts relating to USMA, the U.S. Army, and the profession of arms; admission is free.
cards.source_title: West Point Museum — U.S. Army Center of Military History
cards.access_notes: 2110 New South Post Rd.; listed hours are Tuesday–Sunday, 10:00 a.m.–4:00 p.m.; closed Mondays and specified holidays.

cards.title: Highland Falls Library — books, study areas, and programs
cards.subtitle: Main Street corridor — 298 Main Street
cards.notes: Use the library’s adult study areas, internet computers, catalog, or community-room programming; check its calendar before making a dedicated trip.
cards.short_summary: A Main Street library serving Highland Falls, Fort Montgomery, and West Point courtesy users.
cards.evidence_claim: The library says its 2001 building includes adult book and study areas, internet computers, an online catalog, and a community room for meetings, programs, and art displays.
cards.source_title: History of Our Library — Highland Falls Library
cards.access_notes: 298 Main Street; municipal listing gives Tuesday hours until 7 p.m. and other weekday/Saturday hours.

cards.title: Town Hall — public records and local-government access
cards.subtitle: Main Street corridor — 254 Main Street
cards.notes: Stop during office hours if you need public town documents or want a practical anchor for understanding the Town of Highlands’ local services.
cards.short_summary: The town-government office holding official documents and public records.
cards.evidence_claim: The Town Clerk states that official town documents, including board minutes, agreements, resolutions, Town Code, and local laws, are kept in this office and available to the public.
cards.access_notes: 254 Main Street; Town Clerk hours are listed as Monday–Friday, 8:00 a.m.–4:30 p.m.

cards.title: Hacienda Restaurant — Mexican, Spanish, and Latin American menu
cards.subtitle: Main Street corridor — 145 Main Street
cards.notes: Use the posted menu to choose a pickup, delivery, or dine-in meal, and confirm the day’s service window before heading down Main Street.
cards.short_summary: A Main Street restaurant with Mexican, Spanish, and Latin American dishes.
cards.evidence_claim: Hacienda’s official site lists 145 Main Street and describes its menu as Mexican, Spanish, and Latin American, including enchiladas, chimichangas, quesadillas, and tacos.
cards.access_notes: 145 Main Street; the site lists takeout hours and pickup/delivery ordering.

cards.title: Brother’s Pizza — dine-in or takeout pizza and sandwiches
cards.subtitle: Main Street corridor — 233 Main Street
cards.notes: Choose dine-in or carryout from the pizza, sandwich, calzone, and salad menu; the restaurant says it does not offer delivery.
cards.short_summary: A Main Street pizzeria with dine-in and carryout service.
cards.evidence_claim: Brother’s Pizza lists its Highland Falls location at 233 Main Street and says its menu includes thin-crust and Sicilian pizzas, salads, sandwiches, and calzones.
cards.access_notes: 233 Main Street; listed hours are Monday–Friday 11 a.m.–8 p.m. and Saturday noon–8 p.m.; closed Sunday.

cards.title: Grandma’s Bagels & Pizza — morning-to-evening counter stop
cards.subtitle: Main Street corridor — 265 Main Street
cards.notes: Plan a quick Main Street meal around the posted 7 a.m.–6 p.m. service window, and use the menu for bagels, pizza, sandwiches, or salads.
cards.short_summary: A Main Street shop listing bagels, pizza, and a broad casual-food menu.
cards.evidence_claim: Grandma’s Bagels & Pizza lists 265 Main Street and a menu that includes pizza, salads, sandwiches, calzones, and breakfast items.
cards.access_notes: 265 Main Street; the official ordering site displays 7:00 a.m.–6:00 p.m. service information.

cards.title: Andy’s Restaurant — early breakfast and lunch hours
cards.subtitle: Main Street corridor — 281 Main Street
cards.notes: Use this stop for a daytime meal when the early schedule fits; check the posted holiday caveat before relying on a specific opening time.
cards.short_summary: A Main Street restaurant with early daytime service.
cards.evidence_claim: Andy’s official site lists the restaurant at 281 Main Street and publishes hours beginning at 6:00 a.m., with service ending between 2:00 p.m. and 5:00 p.m. depending on the day.
cards.source_title: Andy's Restaurant — Reviews and Contact Information
cards.access_notes: 281 Main Street; posted hours vary by day and may vary on holidays.

cards.title: West Point Pizza — delivery or Main Street pickup
cards.subtitle: Main Street corridor — 282 Main Street
cards.notes: Use online ordering for pickup or delivery, or visit the Main Street location; the business says it delivers to West Point, Highland Falls, and parts of Fort Montgomery.
cards.short_summary: A Main Street pizza restaurant serving the West Point and Highland Falls area.
cards.evidence_claim: West Point Pizza lists 282 Main Street, states it is open daily from 11 a.m. to 10 p.m., and says it offers delivery to West Point, Highland Falls, and some of Fort Montgomery.
cards.access_notes: 282 Main Street; official site lists daily hours of 11:00 a.m.–10:00 p.m.

cards.title: Bear Mountain Bakery — bakery counter on Main Street
cards.subtitle: Main Street corridor — 307 Main Street
cards.notes: Make this a daytime food stop and verify the day’s hours before leaving; the bakery’s own contact page provides the address and weekly schedule.
cards.short_summary: A bakery at 307 Main Street with published daily hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Bear Mountain Bakery’s official contact page lists its address as 307 Main Street, Highland Falls, and provides hours for each day of the week.
cards.access_notes: 307 Main Street; the business lists 8:00 a.m.–8:00 p.m. Monday–Saturday, with Sunday hours shown separately.

cards.title: The Wintermarket — Saturday produce, flowers, and books
cards.subtitle: Main Street corridor — 401 Main Street
cards.notes: Time this stop for the Saturday indoor market season and browse vendors offering fresh produce, flowers, and books at the stated Main Street location.
cards.short_summary: A seasonal Saturday indoor farmers’ market in Highland Falls.
cards.evidence_claim: The Wintermarket identifies 401 Main Street as its location and says vendors offer fresh produce, flowers, and books; it lists Saturday hours from 10 a.m. to 2 p.m. from November to May.
cards.access_notes: 401 Main Street; listed schedule is Saturdays, 10:00 a.m.–2:00 p.m., November through May.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented West Point rituals and class milestones, from Reception Day to the Army–Navy week traditions.

cards.title: The Cadet Honor Code
cards.subtitle: West Point’s cadet-run honor system
cards.notes: Read the code before visiting or talking with cadets; it anchors daily expectations and has been developed and enforced by cadets for generations.
cards.short_summary: A cadet-led code of honesty that is central to West Point’s character-development system.
cards.evidence_claim: West Point says the Honor Code emerged from cadet efforts in the 1800s and was formalized in the 1920s with the Cadet Honor Committee.
cards.access_notes: This is an institutional tradition and code, not a visitor activity.

cards.title: Ring Weekend
cards.subtitle: Class-ring ceremony at Trophy Point
cards.notes: Look for official Class of 2026 coverage and ceremony photos to see the moment firsties receive rings that represent their West Point class.
cards.short_summary: Firsties receive their class rings in a formal annual ceremony.
cards.evidence_claim: The West Point Association of Graduates reports that Class of 2026 cadets received their West Point class rings during a Trophy Point ceremony in August 2025.
cards.access_notes: Ceremony access and timing are determined by the Academy; use official event information before planning a visit.

cards.entity_name: West Point Association of Graduates Ring Memorial Program
cards.title: The Ring Melt
cards.subtitle: Gold passed from graduates to a new class
cards.notes: Notice the continuity in the ring story: donated graduate rings are melted and their gold is mixed into rings for a following class.
cards.short_summary: A memorial practice that carries donated class-ring gold into new firstie rings.
cards.evidence_claim: WPAOG describes donated graduate rings being melted and mixed with new gold for the following year’s class rings.
cards.access_notes: The Ring Memorial Program is associated with class-ring production; it is not a walk-in visitor program.

cards.title: The 100th Night Show
cards.subtitle: Firsties mark 100 days to graduation
cards.notes: If the show is publicly scheduled, attend as an audience member and expect class-written humor about academy life rather than a formal ceremony.
cards.short_summary: A firstie production that playfully reflects on four years at the Academy.
cards.evidence_claim: The Army states that West Point’s 100th Night Show has been a tradition since 1871 and lets firsties humorously examine their class experience.
cards.source_title: Firsties celebrate 100th Night Weekend with banquet, show
cards.access_notes: The cited show was held at Eisenhower Hall Theatre; public availability varies by year and event schedule.

cards.title: 500 Days and Counting
cards.subtitle: A class milestone before commissioning
cards.notes: Follow the class’s official 500th Night coverage to see its formal dinner format and the class milestone it marks on the path to graduation.
cards.short_summary: A formal class dinner marking roughly 500 days until graduation and commissioning.
cards.evidence_claim: The Army reports that 500th Night began with the Class of 1965 and marks the days remaining until graduation and commissioning.
cards.source_title: West Point LRC prepares food for 4,400 hungry cadets
cards.access_notes: This is a class event; attendance and visitor access are controlled by Academy event organizers.

cards.title: Goats vs. Engineers
cards.subtitle: Army–Navy Week football tradition
cards.notes: Watch official Army–Navy Week coverage for this cadet game, whose teams historically reflect academic standing and whose result fuels friendly lore.
cards.short_summary: A West Point football tradition tied to Army–Navy Week and academic-ranking teams.
cards.evidence_claim: The Army identifies the Goat-Engineer game as an Army–Navy Week tradition dating to 1905, with Goats and Engineers historically organized by class ranking.
cards.source_title: Another Army-Navy tradition honored at West Point
cards.access_notes: The cited game was played at Michie Stadium; game format, access, and scheduling can change.

cards.title: The Prisoner Exchange
cards.subtitle: Exchange students return to their home sections
cards.notes: Watch the pregame exchange if attending the Army–Navy Game; exchange cadets and midshipmen return to cheer with their home academies.
cards.short_summary: A pregame reunion for semester-exchange cadets and midshipmen.
cards.evidence_claim: The Army describes a longstanding pregame tradition in which exchange cadets and midshipmen are formally exchanged and return to their home academy sections.
cards.source_title: West Point cadets take part in 'prisoner exchange' before Army-Navy game
cards.access_notes: This occurs at the Army–Navy Game; tickets, stadium entry, and event procedures are set by game organizers.

cards.title: Spirit Dinner and Bonfire
cards.subtitle: Army–Navy send-off at West Point
cards.notes: Follow the official Army–Navy Week program for any public viewing guidance; the cited observance moved from a cadet dinner to a rally and bonfire.
cards.short_summary: A cadet spirit observance that sends the Army team toward the annual Navy matchup.
cards.evidence_claim: Army reporting describes a traditional Spirit Dinner and Bonfire, including a rally after dinner and a boat-burning send-off before the Army–Navy game.
cards.source_title: Spirit alive at West Point for Army-Navy Game
cards.access_notes: The cited rally was on Daly Field after dinner in Washington Hall; public access and format vary by year.

cards.entity_name: Reporting to the Cadet in the Red Sash
cards.title: Report to the Red Sash
cards.subtitle: Reception Day’s opening test
cards.notes: Observe only through authorized R-Day programming; new cadets report to an upperclass cadet in a red sash as part of their first academy day.
cards.short_summary: A distinctive Reception Day reporting ritual for incoming cadets.
cards.evidence_claim: The Army calls reporting to the cadet in the red sash a renowned part of West Point’s R-Day experience for new cadets.
cards.source_title: Cadet Cadre Take Leadership Reign To Guide Class Of 2027 Through Cadet Basic Training I
cards.access_notes: R-Day programming is for incoming cadets and authorized guests; follow the Academy’s current visitor instructions.

cards.title: Acceptance Day Parade
cards.subtitle: Plebes are recognized after early training
cards.notes: Check the Academy’s current calendar before making plans; this parade recognizes new plebes after they reach an early West Point milestone.
cards.short_summary: A parade recognizing plebes’ first major milestone at West Point.
cards.evidence_claim: The Army reported that the Class of 2026’s Acceptance Day Parade recognized one of the new plebes’ first significant milestones at West Point.
cards.source_title: Class of 2026 cadets rejoice during A-Day Parade
cards.access_notes: Parade attendance and access depend on the Academy’s current event and installation-entry guidance.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at United States Military Academy, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A practical, under-21-safe sequence of named West Point stops: begin with access and orientation, add history and campus landmarks, then close with a scheduled public performance or recreation stop.

cards.title: Start with access details
cards.subtitle: Arrival stop — West Point Visitors Center
cards.notes: Confirm current entry requirements and pick up visitor information before making plans beyond the public-facing museum and visitor area.
cards.short_summary: Use the official visitor hub to orient yourself and confirm installation access.
cards.evidence_claim: The official Army phonebook lists the West Point Visitors Center at 2107 Pershing Center and gives daily hours of 9 a.m.–4:45 p.m.
cards.source_title: U.S. Army Garrison West Point Phonebook
cards.access_notes: Visitors entering the installation must follow current access instructions; the Visitor Control Center is the official source for credentials.

cards.title: See the museum collection
cards.subtitle: Morning stop — beside the Visitors Center
cards.notes: Build in time for the museum’s military-history galleries, then use the adjacent visitor area to decide what public stops fit the day.
cards.short_summary: A free, documented collection stop next to the visitor center.
cards.evidence_claim: The U.S. Army Center of Military History says the West Point Museum is adjacent to the Visitor Center, has free admission, and is open Tuesday–Sunday from 10 a.m.–4 p.m.
cards.access_notes: The museum is closed Mondays, holidays listed by the museum, and the first Tuesday of each month for administrative duties.

cards.title: Take a guided campus orientation
cards.subtitle: Late morning activity — academic and cadet area
cards.notes: If a tour date is available, register through Admissions and use the guide’s campus context to make later landmark stops more meaningful.
cards.short_summary: A scheduled way to learn the Academy’s grounds and academic area.
cards.evidence_claim: West Point Admissions states that it offers guided cadet/academic-area tours when available and that weekend tours are not offered by Admissions.
cards.access_notes: Register in advance; Admissions says its guided tours are unavailable on weekends, federal holidays, and most academic breaks.

cards.title: Pause at Cadet Chapel
cards.subtitle: Early afternoon stop — 722 Derussy Road
cards.notes: Visit during the stated daytime opening window, or attend the Sunday Protestant service if that fits your plans and access status.
cards.short_summary: A named campus chapel with published public service and daily-opening information.
cards.evidence_claim: West Point states that Cadet Chapel is open daily from 8:15 a.m.–4:15 p.m. and that its Sunday Protestant service is open to cadets, faculty, and the public.
cards.access_notes: Sunday Protestant service is listed for 10:30 a.m.; installation access requirements still apply.

cards.title: Walk the cemetery grounds respectfully
cards.subtitle: Afternoon stop — near the Cadet Chapel area
cards.notes: Use a quiet, daylight visit to observe the historic landscape; stay on established public paths and follow any posted installation guidance.
cards.short_summary: A historic named cemetery referenced in Academy visitor and cadet-life information.
cards.evidence_claim: West Point’s cadet-life page identifies the West Point Cemetery as a campus landmark near Subway and Starbucks.
cards.source_title: Day in the Life of a Cadet
cards.access_notes: Treat the cemetery as a solemn site and comply with current installation-access rules.

cards.title: Find the Old Cadet Chapel
cards.subtitle: History stop — West Point Cemetery
cards.notes: Pair this landmark with the cemetery visit and look for the surviving early chapel building rather than treating the stop as a shortcut through restricted areas.
cards.short_summary: A preserved early Academy chapel relocated to the cemetery.
cards.evidence_claim: West Point Press documents that the 1830s chapel was moved piece by piece to the Cemetery in 1910 and became known as the Old Cadet Chapel.
cards.access_notes: View from permitted areas and follow cemetery and installation rules.

cards.title: Head to Trophy Point
cards.subtitle: Late-afternoon landmark — Hudson River overlook
cards.notes: Use this named outdoor setting as a daylight landmark stop, then check the Band calendar for a public performance that matches your visit.
cards.short_summary: A recurring West Point Band concert setting with current event listings.
cards.evidence_claim: The West Point Band’s events page lists Trophy Point concert-series performances in West Point.
cards.access_notes: Check the specific event listing and current installation access guidance before traveling to the site.

cards.title: Add Battle Monument to the walk
cards.subtitle: Landmark stop — Trophy Point area
cards.notes: Use the monument as a short history stop while you are already at Trophy Point, and read the event information before expecting any programmed activity.
cards.short_summary: A named West Point monument used in a current official public-event program.
cards.evidence_claim: The West Point Band’s 2026 Independence Day program lists a reading of the Declaration of Independence at Battle Monument.
cards.access_notes: The cited program was for July 4, 2026; check current event and access information for any visit.

cards.title: Catch a Band performance if scheduled
cards.subtitle: Evening activity — check Trophy Point and other listed venues
cards.notes: Choose a performance from the official calendar, confirm the venue, and arrive through the required access process rather than assuming a concert is on every weekend.
cards.short_summary: A current public-performance option with a direct calendar.
cards.evidence_claim: The West Point Band states that all of its performances are free and open to the public, unless specific event information says otherwise.
cards.access_notes: Tickets are not required unless an individual event page says otherwise; verify the date, venue, weather plan, and access requirements.

cards.title: End with a bowling session
cards.subtitle: Evening stop — near Buffalo Soldier Field
cards.notes: If you have authorized access, make this the indoor finish: check the posted hours first and plan enough time for a lane and a simple snack.
cards.short_summary: An on-post bowling destination with published weekend evening hours.
cards.evidence_claim: West Point’s cadet-life page says the West Point Bowling Alley is near Buffalo Soldier Field and lists Saturday hours of noon–11 p.m. and Sunday hours of noon–7:30 p.m.
cards.source_title: Day in the Life of a Cadet
cards.access_notes: Weekend hours listed by West Point extend to 11 p.m. Saturday and 7:30 p.m. Sunday; confirm entry eligibility and hours before going.

warnings: West Point is an active military installation. Current Army guidance says visitors without Department of War ID need a local-area credential and must comply with access instructions; verify requirements before traveling beyond public-facing areas.
